network.overall_strategy: Pluralistic network integrating seven experimentally demonstrated prebiotic proline routes: (1) electric-discharge synthesis from reduced C/N/H gases; (2) thermal formaldehyde-ammonia chemistry; (3) formaldehyde–hydroxylamine with multicomponent mineral catalysis; (4) hydrothermal HCN/C=O/NH4+ chemistry at mineral surfaces; (5) cyanosulfidic photoredox synthesis via 3-aminopropanal and explicit cyclic N intermediates (Patel route); (6) formamide chemistry under meteorite catalysis and irradiation; (7) UV irradiation in interstellar/pre-cometary ices and subsequent hydrolysis. The network explicitly differentiates the formation of the proline molecular skeleton from subsequent (unresolved) enantioenrichment to L-proline, per best practice in the literature. All major molecules and reaction types experimentally demonstrated to yield proline or its immediate aminonitrile precursor are included, with environmental and geochemical critiques addressed at each step.

reactions.name: Electric discharge synthesis of amino acid precursors from reduced gases

conditions.other: Electric discharge; strong reducing gas mix

reactions.mechanism: Electric discharge breaks down CH4, N2, H2O, NH3 to provide HCN, HCHO, and other reactive C/N fragments, followed by Strecker-type and polymerization chemistry with minor proline branch.
reactions.reasoning: Supported by Ring et al. (1972), Criado-Reyes et al. (2021); proline detected among minor products of discharge, mechanism unresolved. Glass/rock surface increases diversity (Criado-Reyes 2021). Route has atmospheric/chemical critiques, but demonstrates entirety of proline skeleton from C1/C2/C3 precursors.

reactions.name: Thermal condensation of formaldehyde and ammonia (Fox–Windsor route)
reactions.mechanism: Repeated C–C condensation and nitrogen incorporation form polymeric/hydrolysable intermediates, hydrolysis liberates proline along with other amino acids.
reactions.reasoning: Fox & Windsor (1970) and Wolman et al. (1971): amino acid mixture (incl. proline) released after hydrolysis, no mineral catalyst; mechanistically unresolved for the proline ring, but experimentally detected endpoint. Hydrolysis blank controls required; product is not free proline in environment.

reactions.name: Formaldehyde–hydroxylamine condensation with transition metals, MoO4^2−, and clays (Hatanaka–Egami route)
reactions.mechanism: Formaldehyde and hydroxylamine react to give N-rich oligomers, transition metals and molybdate shift selectivity towards proline; hydrolysis releases proline.
reactions.reasoning: Hatanaka & Egami (1977): Proline yield highly molybdate-selective; clays and transition metals cooperative; feedstock concentrations/geochemical plausibility are critiqued. Mechanistic intermediates not resolved. Prebiotic supply of hydroxylamine and Mo debated.

reactions.name: Photochemical cyanosulfidic pathway: HCN and acetylene to acrylonitrile (Patel step 1)
reactions.mechanism: Photoredox/UV-initiated addition of HCN to acetylene yields acrylonitrile as key proline chain precursor.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015): Experimentally established cued by UV; crucial C₂ fragment addition; intermediates tracked.

reactions.name: Acrylonitrile to β-aminopropionitrile
reactions.mechanism: Direct nucleophilic addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile produces β-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015): 83% conversion under experimental conditions. Simple amine addition.

reactions.name: Photoreduction of β-aminopropionitrile to 3-aminopropanal (Patel step 3)
reactions.mechanism: Photochemically driven reduction using H2S yields 3-aminopropanal from β-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015): Mechanistically explicit; redox chemistry by H2S under UV; critical C₃ proline precursor.

reactions.name: Aminopropanal to cyclic thioamide intermediates and proline aminonitrile (Patel final steps)
reactions.mechanism: Cyanohydrin formation, thioamide cyclization, and further photoreduction produces cyclic aminonitrile precursor of proline.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015): All intermediates characterized, thioamide and ring closure demonstrated; mixture of Cu(I) and HS– catalysis; endpoint is pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of proline aminonitrile to racemic proline
reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis at the α-aminonitrile function gives free (DL)-proline.
reactions.reasoning: Standard hydrolysis; precedent in Strecker chemistry; explicit hydrolytic conversion of aminonitrile established in analogous reactions. Not yet implemented by Patel in a continuous prebiotic setting.

reactions.name: Hydrothermal ammonium-cyanide-carbonyl aminating system (Hennet route)
reactions.mechanism: Simultaneous Strecker-type and sidechain-cyclization via C₃–C₅ intermediates; Fe–S/oxide minerals maintain redox; sequence yields mixture of α-amino acids (inc. proline) under hydrothermal gradients.
reactions.reasoning: Hennet et al. (1992): Proline among hydrothermal reaction products from C1/N1 feedstocks in mineral-rich environment. Precursor concentrations higher than likely natural, but environmental chemistry validated. Mechanism for ring closure unresolved.

reactions.name: Irradiated formamide + meteoritic minerals (Saladino route)
reactions.mechanism: Radical-induced polymerization and rearrangement under irradiation followed by hydrolysis liberates amino acids, including proline, from formamide and meteorite mixture.
reactions.reasoning: Saladino et al. (2015): Proline detected uniquely in the irradiation/meteorite/formamide regime. Radical mechanism and product assignments require further isotope study for full mechanistic resolution.

reactions.name: UV-irradiated interstellar/pre-cometary ice (Muñoz Caro, Bernstein routes)
reactions.mechanism: UV creates radical-rich environment in ice, forming complex organic residue; warm-up and hydrolysis releases proline among amino acids.
reactions.reasoning: Muñoz Caro et al. (2002); Bernstein et al. (2002): Isotope-labeled detection; proline among release products. Mechanistic intermediates for proline ring in solid-state are unassigned. Racemic product distribution.

reactions.name: Chiral enrichment (speculative)
reactions.mechanism: Mechanism unresolved; possible stochastic or surface-driven enrichment.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative. As demonstrated in all surveyed routes, prebiotic proline is racemic; no demonstrated L-selective abiotic process. Enantiomeric excess could arise via environmental symmetry breaking but is not yet proven experimentally for L-proline. (Muñoz Caro et al. 2002; Engel & Nagy 1982; see executive assessment)

pathways.name: Electric Discharge (Ring/Miller) Pathway
pathways.description: Reductive discharge of CH4/N2/H2O/NH3 forms small C/N/H organics, HCN, HCHO; nonselective network gives minor yield of proline.

pathways.name: Thermal Formaldehyde–Ammonia (Fox–Windsor) Pathway
pathways.description: Thermal condensation/polymerization of HCHO and NH3 in water at ~185°C, hydrolysis yields proline among other amino acids.

pathways.name: Formaldehyde–Hydroxylamine–Molybdate (Hatanaka–Egami) Pathway
pathways.description: Condensation of formaldehyde and hydroxylamine in mineral/molybdate-rich setting, with hydrolysis yielding proline selectively.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal Cyanide/Carbonyl Pathway (Hennet/Marshall)
pathways.description: FeS mineral-catalyzed hydrothermal chemistry of HCN, HCHO, and NH4+ at 150 °C yields proline through a mixture of Strecker and cyclization.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic Photoredox (Patel) Pathway
pathways.description: HCN + acetylene → acrylonitrile → β-aminopropionitrile → 3-aminopropanal → cyclic thioamide → proline aminonitrile → proline, all under UV/sulfide/copper catalysis.

pathways.name: Formamide-Meteorite Irradiation Pathway (Saladino)
pathways.description: Proline and other amino acids formed by irradiation of formamide with meteoritic catalysts under proton irradiation.

pathways.name: Interstellar-Ice UV Photolysis Pathway (Muñoz Caro/Bernstein)
pathways.description: Solid-state photolysis of N/C-containing ices, followed by warm-up/hydrolysis gives proline among complex mixture.

pathways.name: 3-Aminopropanal Hub Pathway
pathways.description: Alternative formation of 3-aminopropanal from C3 fragments, then conversion via cyclic intermediates to proline (leveraging Patel's intermediates in other settings).

pathways.name: Chemical Network Convergence via β-Aminopropionitrile
pathways.description: Routes converging on β-aminopropionitrile (from acrylonitrile, HCN, formaldehyde, or other prebiotic C/N chains), then proceeding as in the cyanosulfidic photoredox branch.

pathways.name: Speculative Physical/Chemical Enrichment Pathway (Final L-Selection)
pathways.description: Any route yielding racemic proline (mol_019, from rxn_001–rxn_011) followed by speculative chiral enrichment (rxn_012) to L-proline.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The electric discharge (Ring/Miller) pathway is grounded in classic experiments but suffers from low product yields, unresolved mechanism for ring formation, and (per RDKit) significant stoichiometric imbalances (rxn_001 UNBALANCED). The assumed gas mix (CH4/N2/NH3-rich) fits surface discharge experiments but is geochemically contested for Hadean Earth. Detailed downstream intermediates to proline are not mapped. This route is best considered as an endpoint detection, not a mechanistically specified pathway to proline.
suggestions: Clarify mechanistic steps or node sequence leading to proline.
Explicitly indicate necessary atmospheric context for CH4/NH3-rich gas.
Correct or balance stoichiometry for rxn_001.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The Fox–Windsor thermal pathway is experimentally founded but poorly mechanistically resolved. It yields proline after hydrolysis but does not specify the proline precursor. RDKit identifies rxn_002 as severely unbalanced. The high temperature is reasonable for volcanic/hot surface pools, but precursor concentrations and uncharacterized intermediates weaken network validity.
suggestions: Annotate the unidentified hydrolyzable intermediate.
Ensure stoichiometric balancing for rxn_002.
Include hydrolysis explicitly if relevant.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The Hatanaka–Egami pathway captures a mineral-catalyzed, molybdate-sensitive proline-selective experiment. Mechanistically, the pathway from HCHO/NH2OH to proline remains open-ended, with the underlying C–N ring formation unresolved. rxn_003 is unbalanced (both elements and charge). Molybdate concentrations used are geochemically problematic, but the environmental assignment is consistent with laboratory surface chemistry.
suggestions: Balance rxn_003 stoichiometry including MoO4^2- and side-products.
Justify or modulate Mo concentration for plausible early Earth relevance.
Clarify catalytic role and hydrolysis if included.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The Hennet/Marshall hydrothermal route is supported by experiments showing proline among hydrothermal Strecker-like products, but reaction rxn_009 is unbalanced. The pathway lacks mechanistic detail for the proline ring. Environmental conditions are reasonable for hydrothermal vents, but precursor concentrations in experiments were much higher than plausible for bulk settings.
suggestions: Provide mechanistic rationale for ring-forming chemistry.
Balance all atoms in rxn_009.
Discuss precursor concentration realism or propose concentration mechanisms.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Patel's cyanosulfidic pathway closely matches modern mechanistic evidence for proline aminonitrile synthesis. All intermediates are relevant and supported by experiment. However, rxn_006, rxn_007, and rxn_008 are flagged as unbalanced (element and/or charge discrepancies). Environmental assignments (surface with UV, Cu, HS-) are appropriate. The main limitation is the incomplete balancing/annotation of intermediates and the endpoint being DL-proline via hydrolysis, in accord with literature. Environmental integration of all needed components (HCN, acetylene, ammonia, HS-, Cu) is a real-world unresolved issue but chemically justified in context.
suggestions: Balance rxn_006, rxn_007, and rxn_008 with explicit side-products.
Specify the full fate of S, N, O atoms in ring-closure and hydrolysis.
Discuss the plausible geochemical context for coincident delivery of all reagents.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Saladino's formamide + meteorite irradiation route is included correctly as a convergent mechanism, but rxn_010 is unbalanced and the detailed proline ring mechanism is unspecified. The environment (irradiated formamide, meteorite mineral suite) is accurate. Mechanistic detail is lacking for how ring formation proceeds, and the formamide concentration may not be prebiotically realistic.
suggestions: Balance rxn_010, annotate C/N source entry into proline skeleton.
Address mechanism for ring closure or clearly label as 'proline detected post-hydrolysis.'
Comment on formamide plausibility/concentration mechanism.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The interstellar/pre-cometary UV photolysis pathway (Muñoz Caro, Bernstein) is represented faithfully, but rxn_011 is unbalanced. It is accurately flagged as producing DL/proline or its precursors after irradiation and warming/hydrolysis. Feedstocks and astrochemical context are consistent. Mechanistic class (solid-state radical chemistry) is retained, but specific stepwise intermediates are not resolved.
suggestions: Indicate which intermediates (aminonitrile, macromolecular) are hydrolyzed.
Balance rxn_011 for all elements.
Note that enantiomeric excess is not supported in these routes.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The 3-aminopropanal hub pathway is properly constructed in line with explicit proline-precursor formation literature (Patel), integrating plausible synthetic logic. However, multiple constituent reactions are flagged as unbalanced. Environmental assignment is appropriate (surface/UV). Needs structural troubleshooting for atom/charge balance in late C3-to-C5 cyclizations and hydrolysis.
suggestions: Balance all reactions especially the transitions involving ring closure, sulfur, and hydrolysis.
Explicitly indicate side-products and clarify fate of S/N/O atoms.
Preserve clear annotation of aminopropanal derivation as a key hub.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This pathway highlights the network convergence onto β-aminopropionitrile and 3-aminopropanal, reflecting the experimental evidence for these as key intermediates. Multiple unbalanced reactions undermine full chemical feasibility. A strong mechanistic logic is present, but balancing and annotation of all atom flows are necessary. Environmental progression is reasonable.
suggestions: Balance all steps, e.g., S, N, O atom flows.
Clarify fate of every element in cyclization and hydrolysis.
Justify environmental progression through integration of intermediate supply.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The speculative L-selection pathway is appropriately identified as unresolved and not assigned experimental evidence. In line with literature, the network does not claim an established route to L-proline from racemate. The step is marked speculative and does not attempt to encode unsubstantiated chirality, so overall network logic is preserved. Target achievement is low by design.
suggestions: Continue to mark L-enrichment as a separate, speculative module.
Annotate possible physical or chemical symmetry-breaking mechanisms as research advances.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network is pluralistic and comprehensive, faithfully representing the major experimentally demonstrated prebiotic routes to proline and its aminonitrile precursor. All key intermediates and environmental contexts are correctly differentiated and annotated, with appropriate critique of the lack of a geochemically justified route to L-proline. Mechanistic detail for the Patel cyanosulfidic pathway is strong and matches current literature; other routes are properly identified as lacking mechanistic or environmental completeness. The single largest technical problem is the prevalence of unbalanced reaction nodes throughout the network. Nine of twelve reactions are unbalanced (by the deterministic check), including key steps in almost every pathway. Several intermediate formula inconsistencies (esp. C3 species) suggest mistaken annotation or missing byproducts. The network topology, convergence through β-aminopropionitrile and 3-aminopropanal, and explicit assignment of homochirality as a distinct unsolved module are all best practice. Overall, chemical feasibility, pathway logic, and literature alignment are high, but network validity suffers due to unbalanced reactions and some inconsistent intermediate atom counts. Correcting stoichiometry, specifying all byproducts, and updating molecular formulas would raise the confidence to the approval threshold.

formula_mismatches: mol_009 (acrylonitrile): stated formula C3H5N disagrees with its InChI structure (stated minus InChI: H+2)
mol_010 (1,3-diaminopropane): stated formula C3H8N2 disagrees with its InChI structure (stated minus InChI: H-2)
mol_011 (3-aminopropanal (β-aminopropionaldehyde)): stated formula C3H8N2O disagrees with its InChI structure (stated minus InChI: H+1, N+1)
mol_012 (β-aminopropionitrile): stated formula C3H8N2O2 disagrees with its InChI structure (stated minus InChI: H+2, O+2)
